title: Sizes and natural sorting
description:
Two things every file list needs:

```cpp
std::string formatSize(std::uint64_t bytes);
bool naturalLess(const std::string& a, const std::string& b);
```

**formatSize** shows sizes like Explorer: below 1024, `"N bytes"` (`"1 byte"` for one). Otherwise divide by 1024 until the value is below 1024 (at most up to TB), and show **three significant digits, rounded down**, with the unit `KB`, `MB`, `GB` or `TB`: `1536` is `"1.50 KB"`, `10 240` is `"10.0 KB"`, `123 456 789` is `"117 MB"`. Use integer arithmetic so there are no rounding surprises: for example, hundredths are `bytes * 100 / 1024^k`.

**naturalLess** compares like Explorer's `StrCmpLogicalW`: runs of digits are compared as **numbers** (`file2` before `file10`), everything else character by character ignoring case. When two digit runs have the same value, the shorter run comes first (`a01` after `a1`). If everything compares equal, fall back to a plain case-sensitive comparison so the order is total.
hints: For digit runs, skip leading zeros and compare the remaining digits first by length, then as text: no conversion to a number is needed, so even 50-digit runs work.
